text:
Aisha (Sales): Hey team — prospective customer (FinPay) flagged PCI scope. They want a BYO-key HSM PoC but security wants availability/rotation guarantees before legal signs. TL;DR: need clear answers on rotation windows, failover behavior, and what we can commit for the PoC.
Danielle (SE): Quick Qs for the ask: are they expecting hardware HSM in their VPC (CloudHSM) or an external customer HSM that talks to our control plane? That changes network & attestation flow.
Lee (Customer): They have an on-prem Thales HSM. They want to know if Redwood can accept a remote key-proxy or if we require key import into CloudHSM. Also timeline: 3-week PoC target.
Marco (Security): From infosec side: we need to confirm FIPS 140-2/3 level, attestation artifacts (certs), key usage policies (wrap/unwrap only?), and the rotation process — support for scheduled rotations and emergency rotations without service impact.
Jon (Infra Ops): Network gating: if it's on-prem HSM we need an outbound TLS tunnel from customer to our key-proxy endpoint. Ports: TCP 443 outbound, mTLS client certs. We'll need IP allowlist for the PoC and a static egress IP range.
Danielle (SE): For fallback during rotation: we can route requests to a Redwood-managed key variant or a lower-tier model if customer allows. If they insist on no Redwood-managed keys, we can implement a synchronous double-write pattern during the PoC but it increases latency.
Aisha (Sales): Legal asked for SLA language — can we provide an availability commitment specifically for KMS handshake/authorization? They want 99.9% for crypto ops during business hours.
Priya (Legal): 99.9% for the control plane is negotiable, but we need to capture permitted maintenance windows, MTTR for key unavailability, and an explicit statement about key custody (we must clarify if Redwood ever sees key material). Also add indemnity and data breach response timelines.
Marco (Security): Also: rotation proofs. Customer wants proof that rotation happened (signed rotation events). We can emit audit logs and signed rotation statements — need SE to confirm format and retention.
Danielle (SE): We can push an RFC3339 rotation event to audit logs + signed attestation blob (HSM-signed). Example event: `{"event":"rotation","key_id":"cust-key-123","old_kid":"abc","new_kid":"def","ts":"2026-03-18T22:14:00Z"}` — we'll sign that with HSM key.
Lee (Customer): That should work. Also can you confirm impact on throughput during rotation? We need <5% latency variance and no >2s tail p99 increase.
Jon (Infra Ops): During rotation we do atomic metadata swap; for proxyed HSM it adds one extra roundtrip for the first use while caches warm. Plan: warm KV cache and do canary traffic to new key. Expect transient tail increases — we'll target <1.5s p99 delta for the PoC with tuned batching.
Aisha (Sales): Pricing question: how do we bill for HSM-backed ops during PoC? Do we charge per-key, per-call, or flat PoC fee? Customer asking for a predictable PoC cost.
Danielle (SE): For PoC we usually propose a flat engineering + reserved capacity fee for the 3-week window plus metered per-100k crypto ops if they exceed baseline. I'll get numbers for an initial quote.
Priya (Legal): Also need to confirm whether BYO HSM means customer provides HSM network egress only or we host an HSM gateway in their VPC — different liability.
Marco (Security): One more ask: key rotation SLA for emergency rotation (compromise scenario). They want ability to force-rotate within 15 minutes and an automated rollback plan. Do we support forced rotation via API and immediate cutover?
Danielle (SE): We support forced rotation via admin API; cutover depends on caching TTLs. For immediate cutover we can set cache TTL to 0 for the PoC and perform a coordinated deploy; expect small transient rate-limiting until caches repopulate.
Lee (Customer): Ok — their ops team insists on a preflight checklist they can run. Can we give firewall + cert steps and a curl healthcheck example?
Danielle (SE): Example snippet for the preflight healthcheck:
```
curl -v -H "x-redwood-key-id: cust-key-123" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  https://proxy-kms.redwood.example.com/healthz
```
Expect 200 and JSON `{\"status\":\"ok\",\"hsm_connected\":true}`.
Jon (Infra Ops): We'll provide a whitelisted CIDR and a short script to validate TLS handshake with mTLS certs. Also will attach sample iptables rules to the runbook.
Aisha (Sales): Can SE produce the runbook + PoC SOW doc this week? Customer wants to sign off Monday.
Danielle (SE): I'll draft runbook and a concise SOW by EOD Friday. It'll include: scope, test cases (rotation, failure, throughput), acceptance criteria, measurement scripts, and cost for the 3-week PoC.
Priya (Legal): I'll prepare a minimal PoC addendum focusing on custody, SLA, and liability caps to speed signature.
deploy-bot: Created ticket KMS-POC-458 in eng-sre, assigned to Danielle and Jon.
Aisha (Sales): Awesome. Next steps: Danielle to post runbook link here, Jon to confirm IPs and firewall notes, Marco to list attestation artifacts, Priya to draft PoC addendum. Lee — we'll aim for kick on Monday if all ok. :thumbsup:
Lee (Customer): Sounds good. We'll review the runbook and revert. Thanks all.
